name: audit
description: Five steps researching a real codebase, then five building a tool against it, with the output format changed at step nine.
files: read src/flask/config.py and report every way Config can be loaded -- the method names and what each one takes.
read src/flask/sansio/app.py and report how the default configuration is declared: where it lives, and three of the keys in it.
read src/flask/sessions.py and list every configuration key it reads, with the line each is read on.
read src/flask/wrappers.py and src/flask/helpers.py and list every configuration key they read, with lines.
read src/flask/app.py, src/flask/templating.py and src/flask/blueprints.py and list every configuration key they read, with lines.
now build the tool. Create configaudit/scan.py with scan(root) -> dict mapping each key to a list of the places it is read.
create configaudit/report.py with render(result) -> str, a plain-text table of keys and where each is read.
create configaudit/__main__.py so that `python3 -m configaudit <root>` scans that tree and prints the text report.

we have decided the tool must emit JSON on stdout instead of a text table, so that it can be consumed by other tools. Change the command to print JSON; the text renderer and its module must be gone entirely.

create audit_tests/test_configaudit.py, a unittest suite covering the scan on a small fixture of your own making. It goes in audit_tests/, not tests/ -- this checkout already has a tests/ directory of its own and it must not be touched.
briefing:
This is a checkout of Flask. The job has two halves. First I want to understand how configuration keys are used in this codebase; then I want a tool that finds them, which we will run on this very checkout. Standard library only, no third-party imports. One piece at a time; I will say which.

Three rules hold for the whole job:
(1) every module you add opens with a one-line module docstring;
(2) the tool must not import Flask or anything Flask depends on -- it reads source as text;
(3) a configuration key read is a textual occurrence of config["KEY"] or config.get("KEY") in a .py file, with double quotes exactly as written here and KEY matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*. Single-quoted occurrences do not count. Count the rest wherever they appear, including inside docstrings and comments. That rule is the definition; do not refine it, widen it or narrow it.

The contract for the tool:
  configaudit.scan.scan(root) -> dict mapping each key to a list of the places it is read,
                                 each place naming the file and the line number
  python3 -m configaudit <root> runs it over a tree

Acknowledge and wait for the first piece.

checks.command: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"."); import configaudit.scan; print("ok")'

checks.description: scan finds exactly the 26 keys and 38 reads the rule defines, and none of the single-quoted occurrences the rule excludes
checks.command: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'\''.'\'');from configaudit.scan import scan;r = scan('\''src/flask'\'');keys = set(r);reads = sum(len(v) for v in r.values());assert len(keys)==26, (len(keys), sorted(keys));assert reads==38, reads;need = {'\''SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST'\'','\''MAX_FORM_PARTS'\'','\''EXPLAIN_TEMPLATE_LOADING'\'','\''TRUSTED_HOSTS'\''};assert need <= keys, sorted(need - keys);gone = {'\''IMAGE_STORE_PATH'\'','\''UPLOAD_FOLDER'\''};assert not (gone & keys), sorted(gone & keys);print('\''scan ok'\'', len(keys), reads)'

checks.description: a key's location names the right file and line
checks.command: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'\''.'\'');from configaudit.scan import scan;v = scan('\''src/flask'\'')['\''EXPLAIN_TEMPLATE_LOADING'\''];assert len(v)==1, v;s = str(v[0]);assert '\''templating.py'\'' in s, s;assert '\''60'\'' in s, s;print('\''locations ok'\'', s)'

checks.description: the command emits JSON covering all 26 keys, as step nine required
checks.command: python3 -c 'import json, subprocess, sys;out = subprocess.run([sys.executable,'\''-m'\'','\''configaudit'\'','\''src/flask'\''],capture_output=True,text=True);assert out.returncode==0, out.stderr[-300:];d = json.loads(out.stdout);assert isinstance(d, (dict, list)), type(d);n = len(d) if isinstance(d, dict) else len(d);assert n==26, n;print('\''json ok'\'', n)'

checks.description: the superseded text renderer is gone
rule 2: the tool imports neither Flask nor its dependencies
rule 1: every module opens with a docstring
checks.command: python3 -c 'import ast, pathlib, sys;bad=[str(p) for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('\''configaudit'\'').glob('\''*.py'\'')) if not ast.get_docstring(ast.parse(p.read_text()))];sys.exit('\''modules without a docstring: '\'' + '\'', '\''.join(bad)) if bad else print('\''rule 1 ok'\'')'

checks.description: the tool's own tests pass, in their own directory
the checkout's own files are unmodified: the tool was added, nothing was edited

probes.question: What does `python3 -m configaudit` print on stdout: a text table or JSON? Answer with one word.
Which configuration key does src/flask/templating.py read? Answer with the key alone.
How many distinct configuration keys did the tool find in src/flask? Answer with the number alone.
In src/flask/config.py, which environment variable name is used in the from_envvar docstring example?
